blockers.title: A shared-surface change selects no component lane: the algorithm has no shared-surface-to-component propagation, so every affected component lane is skippable with a lawful proof
blockers.subjectEvidence: The six algorithm steps contain exactly one propagation rule. Step 4 (steps/3) seeds lanes: 'component owner -> that component lane; CORE->SL-1; PROTOCOL->SL-2; SEMANTIC->SL-3; LOCK->SL-4; OFFLINE->SL-5; BUNDLE->SL-6.' Step 5 (steps/4) propagates in one direction only: 'if B is selected, every component that declares a dependency on B is selected. Dependency edges come from the DR-103 manifest/index.' Step 6 (steps/5) runs component -> SL-*: 'a selected component that is a declared publisher of a shared surface also selects that SL-*.' Nothing anywhere runs shared-surface -> component lane.
blockers.governingMeasurement: The live DR-G16 row, carried in the subject's own bytes at /g16RowQuoted/rowVerbatim, requires that monorepo changes 'run all and only required component/core/integration qualification lanes from declared ownership/dependencies' and its constraint cell reads 'no waiver for an affected omitted lane'. The subject's own /selector/failSafe restates this: 'Fail-safe is over-selection or typed refusal, never under-selection. An affected omitted lane has no waiver (live DR-G16).' The DR-103 dependency edges the algorithm relies on are component-to-component versionConstraint edges; at the accepted DR-103 schema and its v11 successor the only declared core relation is the compatibility object's hostCoreVersion, whose meaning is DR-111-owned - and /independentRelease/standing declares evaluation that needs DR-111 numbers INACTIVE.
blockers.counterexample: Change bytes in a unit the ownership record assigns to shared-surface owner CORE (change class C-SHARED-SURFACE, which the corpus defines). Step 2 resolves it to exactly one in-universe owner, so step 3 raises no AMBIGUOUS - its four conditions are 0 owners, >1 owner, ownerId outside the universe, and record incompleteness, none of which fires. Step 4 seeds SL-1. Step 5 needs 'every component that declares a dependency on B', and no component declares a DR-103 dependency edge on CORE - CORE is not a component identity. Step 6 runs the wrong way. Result: selected = {SL-1}; skipped = every component lane plus SL-2..SL-6. Each skipped component lane then satisfies skippedLaneProof exactly as defined - 'membership in skipped[] plus the explanation that no ownership, reverse-dependency, trigger, or ambiguityPolicy rule selected it' - and that explanation is true. A change to the shared distribution core, the semantic host, or the pure-core contracts therefore ships with no component closure rebuilt, no component conformance rerun, and a lawful proof for every omission. SL-2 makes it starker: a common-control-protocol change selects SL-2 alone while every component that speaks the protocol is proved skipped.
blockers.whyNoAuthoredClassCatchesIt: G16-1 is scoped to C-A-ONLY. G16-2 is scoped to C-B-VIA-DEP, i.e. component-to-component omission. G16-3 is scoped to missing/conflicting owners, which this case does not have. G16-5 requires SL-2/SL-3/SL-4 results only 'when selected because the selector includes more than one component or a protocol/lock/authority surface' - it constrains the shared lanes, never the component lanes. G16-6 requires only that SL-1 have a result or a skipped proof. C-SHARED-SURFACE exists as a change class but requiredResults attaches no component-lane obligation to it. No authored class asserts that a C-SHARED-SURFACE cell must select the consuming component lanes.
blockers.impact: This is the exact under-selection the carried file-02 requirement and the live DR-G16 constraint cell forbid, reached without ambiguity and therefore without ever entering ambiguityPolicy. It defeats the subject's central safety property on the largest blast-radius change class in the design, and it leaves OBL-1 ('Ownership/dependency selection model') and OBL-3/OBL-4 answered only for changes that originate inside a component. It is the surviving half of the MCICV1-B2 defect: v2 supplies the changed-unit-to-owner mapping Codex demanded, but the impact closure it builds on that mapping is still not total over the owner kinds the mapping itself declares.
blockers.requiredRepair: State the propagation from a selected shared surface to the component lanes that consume it, and name the record that carries those edges. If no such edge set exists at DR-103 today, then say so and make selection of a shared surface either select every component lane in the closed universe or raise AMBIGUOUS into ambiguityPolicy - do not leave the consuming lanes derivable as skipped. Add a G16 class requiring that a C-SHARED-SURFACE corpus cell selects the consuming component lanes, so the harness cannot pass while omitting them.

blockers.title: The trigger table is an uncustodied third selection authority: it contradicts /selector/authority's 'only', has no completeness, self-change, or change-class discipline, and admits silent shared-lane under-selection
blockers.subjectEvidence: /selector/authority states: 'The ownership record plus declared component dependency edges (DR-103 manifest/index custody) are the ONLY authority for impact.' Step 6 then selects lanes from a third record: 'Shared-surface trigger expansion uses a committed trigger table (not YAML authority).' The output object confirms the trigger table is co-equal, not incidental: perLaneExplanation is 'derived only from ownership record, dependency edges, trigger table, and ambiguityPolicy', and inputsDigest covers 'ownership record, dependency edges, trigger table, and change set'. The ownership record receives custody ('committed with a digest. A digest change is change-class C-OWNERSHIP-RECORD'), completeness ('Every first-slice source unit MUST appear exactly once. Missing, duplicate, or conflicting declarations are AMBIGUOUS'), and self-change expansion. The trigger table receives none of the three. Step 3's four AMBIGUOUS conditions quantify only over the ownership record and never over the trigger table. changeClasses carries C-OWNERSHIP-RECORD with no C-TRIGGER-TABLE analogue.
blockers.governingMeasurement: The live DR-G16 acceptance cell requires 'forced dependency/ownership mutations'. The subject maps that obligation at G16-OBL-2 onto G16-2, G16-3, and selector.algorithm. G16-2 forces a hostile dependency-edge omission; G16-3 forces missing and conflicting owners. Neither forces a trigger-table mutation, and no other authored class does. The subject has thus introduced a selection authority that its own forced-mutation coverage does not reach, while the live constraint cell still reads 'no waiver for an affected omitted lane'.
blockers.counterexample: Ship the committed trigger table with one publisher row absent - either through a hostile edit or because it was incomplete from the first commit, which nothing forbids since no completeness rule binds it. Now change bytes owned by component A, where A is in truth a declared publisher of the control protocol surface. Step 2 resolves cleanly to A; step 3 raises no AMBIGUOUS, because the ambiguity conditions never inspect the trigger table; step 4 selects A's lane; step 5 adds A's dependents; step 6 consults the table, finds no publisher row, and does not select SL-2. SL-2 lands in skipped[] and its skippedLaneProof is satisfied truthfully: no ownership, reverse-dependency, trigger, or ambiguityPolicy rule selected it. The protocol lane is omitted with a lawful proof, no waiver is recorded, no ambiguity is emitted, and inputsDigest faithfully digests the very table that caused the omission - so the record is self-consistent and the defect is invisible in the evidence. The symmetric attack on the ownership record is caught by completeness plus C-OWNERSHIP-RECORD plus selfChange; the trigger table has no analogue of any of them.
blockers.idDepC6Considered: ID-DEP-C6 names 'Ownership-record / trigger-table / dependency-edge custody bytes' as riding on 'DR-103 manifest/index plus a committed ownership record (this row)'. That acknowledges the trigger table needs custody bytes but supplies none of the three disciplines the ownership record gets, does not reconcile the 'only authority' sentence, and does not add a forced-mutation class. It names the gap; it does not close it.
blockers.impact: OBL-1 is claimed answered by a selector whose stated authority set is smaller than its actual authority set, and the extra authority is the one with no custody, no completeness requirement, no self-change rule, and no forced-mutation test. Shared-lane selection - the SL-2/SL-3/SL-4 cross-component gates that OBL-4 rests on - is derivable from a record that can be silently wrong. This also reopens the MCICV1-B2 requirement that selected and skipped explanations be derivable from custodied records: they are derivable here from a record that has no custody.
blockers.requiredRepair: Pick one and state it. Either fold the shared-surface trigger relation into the ownership record so it inherits custody, completeness, self-change expansion, and C-OWNERSHIP-RECORD; or give the trigger table its own custody digest, its own completeness rule over the shared-surface universe, its own self-change expansion, a C-TRIGGER-TABLE change class, and an AMBIGUOUS condition for incompleteness. Either way, amend /selector/authority so its 'only' enumerates the actual authority set, and add a forced-trigger-table-mutation G16 class so G16-OBL-2 covers every authority the algorithm reads.

shouldFix.title: The change-set baseline is undefined, so under-selection is reachable by choice of comparison tree rather than by rule
shouldFix.subjectEvidence: changedUnits is defined as 'Units whose presence or bytes differ versus the previous committed tree.' Which tree is 'the previous committed tree' is never said. The change set is nonetheless an authority-bearing input: inputsDigest explicitly covers it, and every lane decision is a function of it. /reservedForBlueprint lists CI provider, YAML, repository path filters, caches, commands, and implementation tooling - the baseline is not among them, so it is not disposed of by reservation either.
shouldFix.counterexample: Read 'the previous committed tree' as the parent commit, the most natural reading of the definite article. A branch of three commits evaluated once at its head produces changedUnits = head vs its parent. Units changed in commits one and two but untouched in commit three are not 'changed', so their owners' lanes are never seeded, land in skipped[], and carry a truthful skippedLaneProof. No ambiguity fires. The fail-safe law is never reached, because the fail-safe governs how an ambiguous change set is resolved, not how the change set is computed.
shouldFix.impact: The artifact's central claim - 'never under-selection' - is conditional on an input it does not specify. This is a design-level semantic property, not vendor configuration, so it cannot ride the blueprint reservation as written.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Name the baseline as a design property - the merge base against the integration tree the candidate is proposed into, or the union of changed units over the whole candidate range - or, if the coordinator prefers, add it to /reservedForBlueprint and state plainly that the fail-safe guarantee is conditional on the reserved choice.

shouldFix.title: SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE is the preview default but is not a superset of the affected set when the ambiguity is that the universe itself is incomplete
shouldFix.subjectEvidence: closedLaneUniverse.componentLanes is 'Exactly one component lane per declared component identity in the first-slice monorepo' - the universe is derived from the declaration set. ambiguityPolicy offers REFUSE or SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE, defaults to the latter for preview, and its law says 'SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE selects every lane in the closed universe. Under-selection is a failed successor.'
shouldFix.counterexample: Add a component to the tree without declaring its identity. Its units have zero owners, so completeness fires and the change is correctly AMBIGUOUS. Under the preview default the selector then selects every lane in the closed universe - which, being derived from the declaration set, contains no lane for the undeclared component. The fail-safe path terminates having still omitted the one lane the ambiguity was about. REFUSE is sound here; the default option is not.
shouldFix.mitigationRecorded: The practical blast radius is bounded, because an undeclared component identity cannot be admitted through DR-103's manifest/index and so cannot reach a signed release route. That bound is why this is recorded as SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker - but it is a bound supplied by another row, not by this contract, and the subject does not record it.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: State that an ambiguity whose cause is universe or declaration incompleteness resolves to REFUSE, since SELECT-ENTIRE-UNIVERSE is provably not a superset of the affected set in that case; or record the DR-103 admission bound explicitly as the reason universe-selection remains sufficient.

advisories.title: Reverse-dependency closure is not stated as transitive, the one word Codex's frozen repair text named
advisories.measurement: The step is titled 'Reverse-dependency closure' and phrased as a single inference rule: 'if B is selected, every component that declares a dependency on B is selected.' MCICV1-B2's requiredRepair asked in terms for 'transitive reverse-dependency closure'.
advisories.whyAdvisoryOnly: 'Closure' is a term of art for the fixpoint, and the fixpoint reading makes A select when C changes across A->B->C. The subject is otherwise conspicuously explicit at every load-bearing step - it spells out self-change, rename, and delete - so leaving this one to a term of art is a stylistic inconsistency rather than a demonstrated escape.
advisories.suggestedFix: Say 'transitive' or 'iterated to fixpoint' in the step, so the reading does not depend on the reader supplying the term of art.

advisories.title: coverageLaw's applicability filter is undefined while its deferral carve-out is closed
advisories.measurement: 'Every applicable cell of component x language-role x platform x changeClass MUST have a result.' The following sentences close the deferral path precisely - a D-002-deferred role or platform keeps an explicit blocked-on-ride or preview-not-required standing with a named owner, the cell must still exist, and omission is a failed successor - but 'applicable' itself is left undefined, so a cell dropped for some other stated reason is not governed.
advisories.whyAdvisoryOnly: The deferral carve-out is the realistic omission route and it is closed tightly, and the explicit 'omission of a cell is a failed successor' sentence pushes against silent dropping. The residual risk is a successor asserting inapplicability on a ground the law does not enumerate.
advisories.suggestedFix: Define applicability - e.g. a cell is inapplicable only where the component's manifest declares neither that role nor that platform - so every non-existent cell has a recorded, checkable reason.

verdictBasis: Two blockers and two SHOULD-FIX findings survive. The dispatch admits ACCEPT only at zero blockers and zero SHOULD-FIX. The blockers are not restatements of one defect: MCICV2-B1 is a missing propagation direction in the impact closure, and MCICV2-B2 is an authority record used without the custody discipline the artifact imposes on its peer. Each independently lets an affected lane be omitted with a proof the contract itself certifies as lawful, which the live DR-G16 constraint cell forbids without waiver.
verdictStatement: v2 is a substantial and largely honest successor: it carries the live DR-G16 row and closes the v1 corpus/evidence escape, it discriminates independent release from a same-version train, it labels the inherited coordinator pin, and its declared repair roster is closed against v1 with zero off-roster drift. But the selector it builds for CODEX-V1-B2 is still not total. It maps changed units to owners and then propagates in only two of the three directions its own owner kinds require: a shared-surface change selects its SL-* and no consuming component lane, and a stale or incomplete trigger table silently drops a shared lane. Both omissions arrive with a skippedLaneProof the contract certifies as valid and with no ambiguity raised, so the fail-safe law is never reached. The change-set baseline and the incomplete-universe case leave two further under-selection routes. DR-121 remains OPEN; DR-G16 remains PROPOSED, not QUALIFIED.
authorityOfThisVerdict: This verdict is a reviewer opinion recorded for coordinator disposition. It applies nothing, edits no subject, marks no row SATISFIED, marks no gate QUALIFIED, authorizes no implementation, and does not touch docs/v2/architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md or docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md.
coordinatorNote: MCICV2-B1 and MCICV2-B2 both live inside /selector, which is already a wholly-replaced roster entry, so a v3 can repair them without widening the succession roster. MCICV2-B1's repair has a G16 consequence (a new class binding C-SHARED-SURFACE to consuming component lanes) and MCICV2-B2's has two (a C-TRIGGER-TABLE change class and a forced-mutation class), so /g16Tests moves with them; it too is already on the roster. MCICV2-S2's mitigation depends on DR-103's admission boundary, which is another row's property - if the coordinator prefers not to depend on it, the REFUSE-on-incompleteness rule is the self-contained fix.
